===Etymology 1===
{{wikidata lexeme|L42}}
{{etymon|en|id=response|:inh|enm:answere<id:noun>|tree=1}}
{{root|en|ine-pro|*h₂en-}}
{{root|en|ine-pro|*h₂ent-|*swer-|id2=swear}}
From {{inh|en|enm|answere}}, {{m|enm|andsware}}, from {{inh|en|ang|andswaru||answer}}, from {{af|ang|and-|t1=against|swaru|t2=affirmation|nocat=1}}, (from {{der|en|ine-pro|*h₂ent-||front, forehead}} and {{der|en|ang|swerian||to swear}}, from {{der|en|ine-pro|*swer-}}), suggesting an original meaning of "a sworn statement rebutting a charge". The cognates suggest the existence of {{der|en|gem-pro|*andaswarō||a reply to a question}}. Cognate with {{cog|ofs|ondser||answer}}, {{cog|osx|andswōr||answer}}, {{cog|da|-}} and {{cog|sv|ansvar||liability, responsibility, answer}}, {{cog|is|andsvar||answer, response}}. Compare also {{cog|ang|andwyrde||answer}} (cognate to {{cog|nl|antwoord}}, {{cog|de|Antwort}}), {{cog|ang|andcwiss||reply}}, {{cog|de|Schwur||oath, vow}}.

====Noun====
{{en-noun}}

# A [[response]] or [[reply]]; something [[say|said]] or [[do|done]] in [[reaction]] to a [[statement]] or [[question]].
#: {{syn|en|replication|q1=formal}}
#: {{ux|en|Her '''answer''' to his proposal was a slap in the face.}}
#* {{RQ:Time|author=Rachel Konrad and Matt Abrahams|title=Why Young People Are Struggling to Communicate|date=Dec 9 2025
|text=When a student types a complex question into a chatbot, they get a polished (though not necessarily authentic, accurate or nuanced) '''answer''' in seconds.}}
# A [[solution]] to a problem.
#: {{uxi|en|There is no simple '''answer''' to corruption.}}
#: {{uxi|en|Violence is not the '''answer''' to disagreements.}}
# {{lb|en|after a possessive|with [[to]]}} Someone or something that fills a similar role or position.
#* {{quote-journal|en|date=03 Dec 77|volume=5|number=22|journal=Gay Community News|page=2|title=England's Bryant|text=Anti-pornography crusader Mary Whitehouse, who successfully brought London's ''Gay News'' to trial recently on charges of "blasphemy," is emerging as England's '''answer''' to Anita Bryant.}}
# {{lb|en|legal}} A [[document]] filed in response to a [[complaint]], responding to each point raised in the complaint and raising [[counterpoint]]s.

===Etymology 2===
{{wikidata lexeme|L961}}
{{etymon|en|id=to respond|:inh|enm:answeren|tree=1}}
From {{inh|en|enm|answeren}}, {{m|enm|andswaren}}, {{m|enm|answerien}}, from {{inh|en|ang|andswarian}}, {{m|ang|answarien||to answer, to respond, to deny an allegation under oath}}, from {{inh|en|gem-pro|*andaswarōną}}, {{m|gem-pro|*andaswarjaną||to answer, to give a response, to rebut}}, from {{prefix|gem-pro|*anda|t1=against|*swarjaną|nocat=1}}, {{m|gem-pro|*swarōną||to swear an oath, to answer, to respond}}, from {{der|en|ine-pro|*h₂ent-||face, forehead}} and {{m|ine-pro|*swer-||to swear}}. Cognate with {{cog|ofs|ondswera||to answer}}, {{cog|da|ansvare||to answer, account for}}, {{cog|sv|ansvara||to answer, account for}}, {{cog|is|andsvara||to answer, reply}}.

====Verb====
{{en-verb}}

# {{lb|en|ambitransitive}} To make a reply or response to.
#* {{RQ:Shakespeare Venus and Adonis|passage=She '''answers''' him as if she knew his mind:}}
#* {{RQ:KJV|1 Kings|18|26|passage={{...}} there was no voice, nor any that '''answered'''.}}
#* {{RQ:Churchill Celebrity|chapter=4|passage=“Well,” I '''answered''', at first with uncertainty, then with inspiration, “he would do splendidly to lead your cotillon, if you think of having one.” ¶ “So you do not dance, Mr. Crocker?” ¶ I was somewhat set back by her perspicuity.}}
#: {{ux|en|He '''answered''' the question.}}
# {{lb|en|transitive}} To speak in defence against; to reply to in defence.
#: {{co|en|to '''answer''' a charge or accusation}}
# {{lb|en|ambitransitive}} To respond to a call by someone at a door or telephone, or other similar piece of equipment.
#: {{ux|en|She '''answered''' the door.}}
#: {{ux|en|Nobody '''answered''' when I knocked on the door.}}
# {{lb|en|ambitransitive}} To suit a need or purpose satisfactorily.
#: {{ux|en|It '''answers''' the need.}}
#* {{RQ:Austen Emma|volume=III|chapter=6|passage=Mr. Knightley had done all in his power for Mr. Woodhouse’s entertainment. Books of engravings, drawers of medals, cameos, corals, shells, and every other family collection within his cabinets, had been prepared for his old friend, to while away the morning; and the kindness had perfectly '''answered'''.}}
#* {{quote-book|en|year=1864|author=Joseph Sheridan Le Fanu|title=w:Uncle Silas|passage=Inexperienced girl as I was, I fired at the idea of becoming his dupe, and fancying, perhaps, that there was more in merely answering his note than it would have amounted to, I said — "That kind of thing may '''answer''' very well with button-makers, but ladies don't like it. {{...}}}}
#* {{quote-book|en|year=1871|author={{w|Alexander John Ellis|Alexander J. Ellis}}|title=On Early English Pronunciation|location=London|publisher=Trübner & Co.|section=Part III, Chapter 7, section 1, p. 656, footnote 1|url=https://archive.org/details/onearlyenglishpr03elliuoft
|passage=Of course for publication in a newspaper, my palaeotype would not '''answer''', but my glossotype would enable the author to give his Pennsylvania German in an English form and much more intelligibly.}}
#* {{quote-book|en|year=1903|author={{w|Samuel Butler (novelist)|Samuel Butler}}|title=w:The Way of All Flesh|chapter=41|passage=Theobald spoke as if watches had half-a-dozen purposes besides time-keeping, but he could hardly open his mouth without using one or other of his tags, and "'''answering''' every purpose" was one of them.}}
# To be [[accountable]] or [[responsible]]; to make [[amends]].
#: {{syn|en|answer for}}
#: {{ux|en|The man must '''answer''' to his employer for the money entrusted to his care.}}
#: {{ux|en|He has a lot to '''answer''' for.}}
#* {{RQ:Shakespeare Henry 5|act=IV|scene=viii|page=90|column=2|passage=And pleaſe your Maiestie, let his Neck '''anſwere''' for it, if there is any Marſhall Law in the World.}}
# {{lb|en|legal}} To file a document in response to a [[complaint]].
# To [[correspond]] to; to be in [[harmony]] with; to be in [[agreement]] with.
#* '''1775''', {{w|Richard Brinsley Sheridan}}, ''{{w|The Duenna}}'', Dublin: G. Burnet ''et al.'', 1794, Act II, Scene 2, p. 25,<sup>[http://name.umdl.umich.edu/004835563.0001.000]</sup>
#* {{quote-book|en|year=1793|author={{w|Bryan Edwards (politician)|Bryan Edwards}}|title=The History, Civil and Commercial, of the British Colonies in the West Indies|location=Dublin|publisher=Luke White|section=Volume II, Book V, Chapter 2, p. 231|url=https://catalog.hathitrust.org/Record/100268998
|passage=The use of [[dunder]] in the making of rum, '''answers''' the purpose of yeast in the fermentation of flour.}}
#* {{quote-journal|en|date=29 Dec 79|volume=7|number=23|journal=Gay Community News|page=5|author=John Millea|title=Media Madness|text=Before I knew about sex, I knew that the word queer was an insult associated with skiny boys who couldn't throw a football, and since I '''answered''' this description, I took my share of abuse.}}
# To be opposite, or to act in opposition.
#* {{quote-book|en|year=1786|author={{w|William Gilpin (priest)|William Gilpin}}|title=Observations, relative chiefly to picturesque beauty, made in the year 1772: on several parts of England; particularly the mountains, and lakes of Cumberland, and Westmoreland|location=London|publisher=R. Blamire|section=Volume II, Section 19, p. 85|url=http://name.umdl.umich.edu/004863362.0001.002
|passage=The windows '''answering''' each other, we could just discern the glowing horizon through them {{...}}}}
# To be or act in conformity, or by way of accommodation, correspondence, relation, or proportion; to conform; to correspond; to suit; usually with ''to''.
#* {{RQ:Shakespeare Measure|act=III|scene=i|page=72|column=2|passage={{...}} that the time may haue all ſhadow, and ſilence in it: and the place '''anſwere''' to conuenience}}
#* {{RQ:Shakespeare Pericles|act=V|scene=i|page=69|passage=If this but '''answer''' to my just belief, / I’ll well remember you.}}
#* {{RQ:KJV|Proverbs|27|19|passage=As in water face '''answereth''' to face, so the heart of man to man.}}
#* {{RQ:Swift Gulliver's Travels|part=I|page=36|passage={{...}} I might carry about me several Weapons, which must needs be dangerous things, if they '''answered''' the Bulk of so prodigious a Person.}}
# To respond to satisfactorily; to meet successfully by way of explanation, argument, or justification; to refute.
#* {{RQ:KJV|Matthew|22|46|passage={{...}} no man was able to '''answer''' him a word, neither durst any man from that day forth ask him any more questions.}}
#* {{RQ:Milton Samson|passage=These shifts refuted, '''answer''' thy appellant / Though by his blindness maim’d for high attempts, / Who now defies thee thrice to single fight,}}
#* {{RQ:Macaulay History of England|volume=III|chapter=14|page=354|passage=The reasoning was not and could not be '''answered'''.}}
# To be or act in compliance with, in fulfillment or satisfaction of, as an order, obligation, or demand.
#: {{ux|en|He '''answered''' my claim upon him.}}
#: {{ux|en|The servant '''answered''' the bell.}}
#* {{RQ:Shakespeare Henry 4-1|act=I|scene=iii|passage={{...}} this proud king {{...}} studies day and night / To '''answer''' all the debts he owes unto you}}
# {{lb|en|obsolete}} To render account to or for.
#* {{RQ:Shakespeare Henry 4-1|act=II|scene=iv|passage={{...}} I will, by to-morrow dinner-time, / Send him to '''answer''' thee, or any man, / For any thing he shall be charged withal:}}
# {{lb|en|obsolete}} To atone for; to be punished for.
#* {{RQ:Shakespeare Julius Caesar|act=III|scene=ii|passage={{...}} The noble Brutus / Hath told you Caesar was ambitious: / If it were so, it was a grievous fault, / And grievously hath Caesar '''answer’d''' it.}}
# {{lb|en|obsolete}} To be or act as an equivalent to, or as adequate or sufficient for; to serve for; to repay.
#* {{RQ:KJV|Ecclesiastes|10|19|passage=A feast is made for laughter, and wine maketh merry: but money '''answereth''' all things.}}
